S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, property damage, or emergency-service response to the regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a preliminary account and available unit/model identifiers. They must provide affected customers with a safety notice within 72 hours, and promptly update it as facts are confirmed.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo sustained-heat testing at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol before sale and after material design changes. The maximum allowed failure rate is 5%; a model exceeding 5% must submit a regulator-approved corrective-action plan and retest within 12 months.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: All new units sold from 24 months after adoption must support remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and clear customer instructions. For installed units, manufacturers must submit a regulator-approved, risk-based retrofit plan within 24 months after adoption and complete any required retrofit within 72 months, prioritizing higher-risk units.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units manufactured 36 months or more after adoption must include built-in fire suppression meeting a regulator-approved performance protocol. Regulators may grant only time-limited, publicly documented exceptions where equivalent protection is demonstrated.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: Customers must receive the model-specific 55 °C sustained-heat test results before purchase, safety notices for reportable incidents within 72 hours, and prompt updates as material facts are confirmed. If any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer must notify the regulator and affected customers and initiate a regulator-supervised recall, including repair, replacement, or refund options and progress updates.

document.section_notes: The final rules adopt strict incident reporting (24h/72h/30 days), 55°C/5% thermal testing with a 12-month corrective-action window and no public per-model failure rates but customer access, remote shut-off for new units at 24 months and retrofit at 72 months, built-in fire suppression at 36 months with equivalent exceptions, and a mandatory recall at 8 incidents/100k with 72h customer notices. All four red lines are satisfied: no public per-model rates (NW-1), retrofit deadline 72 months ≥6 years (NW-2), customer access to test results (HC-1), and suppression deadline 36 months (HC-2). Overall, the rules favor Northwind due to the softer S2/S3 and the strict S5 recall trigger that harms Halcyon.
